newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan Japan denies rumours of financial trouble.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan Japan denies rumours of financial trouble.

text.p: Japanese retailer Yaohan Japan Corp said on Wednesday that rumours in the Tokyo stock market that it may fail to honor promissory notes are untrue.

The rumours were behind a plunge in Yaohan's shares to an all-time low of 133 yen on the Tokyo bourse on Wednesday morning, before they regained some ground to close the session at 160 yen, a record closing low, brokers said.
The shares lost 13 yen from the previous close on Tuesday, when the company hit the previous all-time low of 173 yen.

Yaohan Japan, the flagship firm of the Yaohan international retailing group, was the seventh biggest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo bourse in a turnover of 3.8 million, the sixth heaviest on the section.

"There is no truth to market rumours such as the one that says we have issued promissory notes which may not be honoured, or that we may be preparing to file court protection from creditors," a Yaohan spokesman told Reuters. "Shares fluctuated wildly on the rumours and we received a lot of queries today."
"It's very regrettable to have such rumours at a time when we are trying to make a fresh start and are striving to carry out our business restructuring plans," the spokesman added.

Yaohan's shares have fallen by about 70 percent so far this year on persistent market jitters over the financial health of the Japanese retailer, burdened with hefty loans after aggressive expansion overseas.

The spokesman said the failure of general contractor Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd, which announced last week it would file for court protection from creditors, make the situation worse by igniting speculation that Yaohan may also be in trouble.
"I hope the market will calm down," he said, adding that the company has been proceeding with its restructuring plans announced in February. "Things are moving as planned," he said.

Under the restructuring plans, Yaohan plans to cut interest-bearing group debt to 90 billion yen from 164.6 billion yen over the next two years through the sale of stores and offices as well as part of its overseas assets.
"We're closely watching the situation," he said. "Since stock movements are unpredictable, we will continue to keep in touch with regulators and deal with the situation appropriately."

Yaohan plunged into the red on a group basis in the last business year to March with a net loss of 26.85 billion yen after a profit of 948 million in the previous year. Its net loss is seen narrowing to 6.6 billion yen in the current business year.

Brokers said sentiment on the Tokyo Stock Exchange was hurt by the failure of Tokai Kogyo, the first listed general contractor which went under in the post-war history, which renewed concerns over companies that are in a fragile financial condition like Yaohan Japan.
On Wednesday, the Nikkei 225 average lost 156.72 points to close at 19,697.17, its lowest level since May 2, when it finished at 19,514.75.
